question: Your team runs Claude Code with the -p flag in CI to draft release-note entries from merged pull requests, extracting fields such as change type, breaking-change flag and affected module. Entries with high field-level confidence are published without human review. Before launch, the team validated accuracy by change type and module against a labeled set, and every segment performed well. The codebase and its pull request styles keep changing. Which plan best keeps the published entries trustworthy over time?

options.text: Each release, have reviewers check only the high-confidence entries whose scores sit just above the threshold, because these entries are the most likely to be wrong, and publish higher-scoring entries unchecked.
options.reason: This sample is not random across the high-confidence entries. Errors in entries with the highest scores are never measured, so the guide's goals of measuring the error rate and detecting novel patterns are not met.

options.text: Stop human review of high-confidence entries, because the launch validation already showed accurate results for every change type and module.
options.reason: The guide calls for ongoing error rate measurement of high-confidence extractions. A one-time launch check cannot detect error patterns that appear later as the inputs change.

options.text: Each release, re-run the original labeled validation set through the pipeline and stop automatic publishing if its accuracy drops below the launch result.
options.reason: A fixed validation set contains only the old inputs. It cannot reveal novel error patterns in new pull requests, which the guide says stratified random sampling of high-confidence extractions is meant to detect.

options.text: Each release, have reviewers check a stratified random sample of high-confidence entries across change types and modules to track the error rate and spot new error patterns.
options.reason: The guide recommends stratified random sampling of high-confidence extractions for ongoing error rate measurement and novel pattern detection. Stratifying by change type and module keeps every segment represented in each sample.
